routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names no main language. The already selected Danish route remains a complete current published language path and is retained independently of UCR fit; Norwegian and Swedish alternatives are not stacked.

exception.reason: Three independently organised directions were tested. Scandinavian language, linguistics and culture fails because UCR offers no Danish, Norwegian or Swedish acquisition, grammar, sociolinguistics, translation or source-language study. Scandinavian literature, cultural history and Nordic identity has transferable literary, myth, media and cultural-analysis methods, but only an isolated treatment of Norse myth and no sustained Scandinavian literature, cultural history or region-specific research sequence. Nordic societies, politics and northern-European history has genuine comparative politics, sociology, European studies and modern-history frameworks, but no Scandinavian area-studies spine or sustained teaching of Nordic political institutions, welfare systems, societies or modern regional history. In every direction, extending adjacent material to 23 non-PPD courses would change the object of study to general European studies or global humanities. The missing language and regional content are academic substance rather than professional qualification, so no complete UCR response is claimed.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions or outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and Fall-2026-start availability. MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature includes Norse myth within a global comparative course, but UCR has no course in Scandinavian literature, Nordic literary history or region-specific textual interpretation. GOSPOLI112 Foundations of Comparative Politics uses Sweden as one brief example while teaching general comparative institutions, democracy, populism and globalisation; GOSPOLI311, GOSPOLI212, GOSPOLI313 and GOSLAWJ312 add EU, international-relations, conflict and legal frameworks without a Nordic regional sequence. GOSHIST111/211/312 and GOSSOCI111/212/214/311 provide broad modern, imperial, research-historical and sociological foundations, but no course centres Scandinavia, Nordic welfare systems, northern-European modern history or Nordic identity. MCCLITR111/112/212/311/312, MCCCOMM111/211/213/311/312, MCCMEDI111/112/211/311/312 and HCBCOGN312 supply literary, rhetorical, media and psycholinguistic methods, but no Danish, Norwegian or Swedish instruction, Scandinavian linguistics, translation or source-language study. The workbook therefore lacks the language and regional-content core required for a coherent 24-course response.

candidateAssessment.assessment: Psycholinguistics, rhetoric, stylistics, media and qualitative research provide transferable analytic methods, but UCR teaches none of Danish, Norwegian or Swedish and has no Scandinavian grammar, sociolinguistics, mutual-intelligibility, translation or source-language sequence. Those methods cannot supply the languages and regional cultural object that organise this direction.

candidateAssessment.concept: Scandinavian literature, cultural history and Nordic identity
candidateAssessment.assessment: Literary studies, myth, film, media and art-history courses provide genuine interpretive methods, and World Myth & Literature includes Norse myth as one comparative strand. UCR nevertheless has no sustained Scandinavian literature, Nordic cultural or intellectual history, region-specific media, national-identity sequence or independent Scandinavian research. Filling a complete programme would turn it into global literature and cultural studies.

candidateAssessment.concept: Nordic societies, politics and northern-European history
candidateAssessment.assessment: Comparative politics, EU politics, sociology, modern history and qualitative research provide relevant frameworks, and Foundations of Comparative Politics briefly uses Sweden as an example. Their documented content does not teach Nordic political systems, welfare models, contemporary Scandinavian societies, northern-European regional history or Nordic area-studies methods, so expanding them to 23 non-PPD courses would produce generic European social science.
